introduction: On this Sunday, a woman of Shunem welcomes the prophet Elisha into her home and is blessed with a son. In the Gospel, Jesus says that whoever loses their life for his sake will find it, and that whoever welcomes his disciples welcomes him; even a cup of cold water will be rewarded. Paul tells us that in Baptism we died with Christ and rose to new life. Let us welcome Christ in others.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, we have been baptized into Christ's death and raised to new life. Let us bring our prayers to the Father.
intentions: For the Church: that she may welcome all people with the hospitality of the woman of Shunem. Let us pray to the Lord.
For priests, missionaries and all who are sent in Christ's name: that they may be welcomed and supported. Let us pray to the Lord.
For families: that their love for one another may be rooted in their love for Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are thirsty, poor or in need: that they may receive even a cup of cold water in Christ's name. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may live as people dead to sin and alive to God in Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, whoever welcomes your disciples welcomes your Son. Give us generous and hospitable hearts, and help us to lose our lives for him, so that we may find them. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: A cup of cold water
reflection.body:
A wealthy woman in Shunem notices the prophet Elisha passing by and invites him to eat. Then she says to her husband, "I perceive that this is a holy man of God who passes by us continually." She builds a small room on the roof with a bed, a table, a chair and a lamp, so he can stay whenever he comes. Elisha asks how he can repay her, and learns that she has no son. He promises her one. Her generous hospitality is rewarded beyond what she could imagine.

In the Gospel, Jesus speaks strong words about discipleship: "He who loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me." Following him means putting him first, even above those we love most. "He who doesn't take his cross and follow after me isn't worthy of me." Then comes the paradox: "He who seeks his life will lose it; and he who loses his life for my sake will find it."

Jesus then turns to hospitality: "He who receives you receives me, and he who receives me receives him who sent me." Welcoming Christ's messengers is welcoming Christ himself, and the Father. Even the smallest act counts: "Whoever gives one of these little ones just a cup of cold water to drink in the name of a disciple, most certainly I tell you, he will in no way lose his reward."

Paul explains where this new way of living begins: in Baptism. "all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death," so that "we also might walk in newness of life." We are to consider ourselves "dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus our Lord."

This week, practice hospitality like the woman of Shunem: invite someone to your table, welcome a newcomer to your parish, or give a cup of water, literally or figuratively, to someone in need. In them, you welcome Christ.
